notes: tomcat:tomcat and admin:admin land constantly - always try defaults before a full wordlist. Manager creds live in tomcat-users.xml, which Ghostcat can sometimes read without auth.

recommended.note: Deploy a WAR webshell with the cracked creds.
Deploy a msfvenom reverse-shell WAR instead.

name: Tomcat - Manager Brute Force (Metasploit)
description: Brute-forces the Tomcat Manager/Host-Manager HTTP Basic auth using default credential lists. Manager access allows WAR deployment for RCE.

defense.why_it_works: Tomcat's /manager/html endpoint uses HTTP Basic Authentication backed by tomcat-users.xml. Default installs use weak credentials (admin:admin, tomcat:tomcat). No lockout policy is configured by default.
defense.prerequisites: Network access to /manager/html. No lockout policy. Weak or default credentials in tomcat-users.xml.
defense.impact: Manager access enables WAR deployment -- complete server takeover via uploaded webshell or reverse-shell WAR.
defense.detection: High-volume 401 responses followed by 200 to /manager/html. Rapid Basic Auth attempts from one IP. Tomcat access log showing manager authentication failures.
defense.artifacts: Tomcat access_log showing 401s to /manager | catalina.out authentication failure entries | IDS alert for HTTP Basic Auth brute force
defense.prevention: Change default manager credentials. Restrict /manager to localhost via RemoteAddrValve. Implement lockout via reverse proxy. Require client certificate in high-security environments.
defense.misconfiguration: tomcat-users.xml has manager-gui role assigned to default credentials. /manager accessible from all IP addresses without lockout.
defense.vulnerable_config:
<!-- tomcat-users.xml default -->
<role rolename="manager-gui"/>
<user username="tomcat" password="tomcat" roles="manager-gui"/>
<user username="admin" password="admin" roles="manager-gui,admin-gui"/>
defense.secure_config:
<!-- Strong unique credential -->
<user username="mgr_ops" password="(strong-random-pass)"
      roles="manager-script"/>
<!-- context.xml for manager -->
<Valve className="org.apache.catalina.valves.RemoteAddrValve"
       allow="127\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+"/>
defense.evasion: Undeploy the malicious WAR after getting a shell; name it innocuously; manager access over a valid session looks like admin activity.
